object_description: simple flat two-storey volume enclosing an entrance courtyard
design_condition: Set slightly back from the avenue and fitted between the neighboring halls, the volume creates a clear entrance courtyard but leaves little recreational space between the buildings and relies on multiple level changes for access.

positive.statement: The large open courtyard brings all entrances together clearly and forms the center of the department.

position.rationale: Central rectangular courtyard is clearly visible in plan, with surrounding entrance circulation at ground level.

positive.statement: The inviting entrance design and central courtyard provide good lighting and orientation.

position.rationale: Central courtyard and adjacent ground-level openings provide the most plausible entrance and orientation anchor.

positive.statement: The individual functional areas are well separated in the building.

position.rationale: Interior separation is not distinguishable; distributed across the compact two-storey envelope.

positive.statement: The operational organization is well developed.

position.rationale: Operational assessment has no specific geometric referent in the sampled exterior model.

positive.statement: The restrained and simple structure has a quiet appearance.

position.rationale: Uniform compact massing and flat roof are consistently visible across plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The reduced glazing proportion is an advantage for the sustainability standard.

position.rationale: Sparse facade openings are most legible on the south and east elevations.

negative.statement: The building fills the available land between the neighboring halls, leaving little recreational quality between them.

position.target: little recreational quality between neighboring halls
position.rationale: The building nearly fills its rectangular footprint, leaving narrow residual strips along the sides.

negative.statement: The different first-floor levels are barely manageable and create unnecessary obstacles for access and deliveries.

position.rationale: Level changes are not explicit, so the upper-floor circulation zone is approximated within the stepped access envelope.

negative.statement: The entrance to the upper floor is confusing and narrow, while the main staircase is spatially unappealing.

position.target: entrance to upper floor and main staircase
position.rationale: Upper access is interior and indistinguishable; anchored near the central courtyard-facing circulation edge.

negative.statement: The access and front zones to the lecture and seminar rooms are insufficiently dimensioned.

position.target: access and front zones to lecture and seminar rooms
position.rationale: Room fronts are absent from the sample; approximate them along the upper-level perimeter.

negative.statement: The cafeteria is too peripheral to serve as a meeting point and departmental center.

position.rationale: Cafeteria is not identifiable; peripheral ground-level placement reflects the stated criticism.

negative.statement: The western exterior space is completely sealed off and degenerates into a residual space.

position.rationale: Western residual exterior strip is anchored directly outside the building's west edge.

negative.statement: The summer heat insulation has not been sufficiently demonstrated.

position.rationale: Thermal performance is unrepresented; constrained to the sun-exposed south envelope.

negative.statement: The underfloor heating alone is insufficient for the gymnasium temperature regime.

position.rationale: Gymnasium is not distinguishable; approximate a ground-level peripheral room.

negative.statement: Rooms with high internal heat loads are not equipped with additional cooling systems.

position.target: rooms with high internal heat loads
position.rationale: Cooling systems are unrepresented; anchor the estimate to upper-level occupied perimeter zones.
